item.title: More Americans now support than oppose all-day school cellphone bans
item.dc:creator: Beshay
item.description: Three-quarters of U.S. adults support in-class school cellphone bans, and for the first time, more now support than oppose all-day bans for middle and high schoolers.

item.dc:creator: Beshay
item.description: Most Americans support term limits, campaign spending caps, and Electoral College reform, but achieving these changes likely would require amending one of the world's hardest constitutions to change.

item.dc:creator: Beshay
item.description: U.S. foreign aid fell to its lowest inflation-adjusted level in over two decades in fiscal 2025, dropping to $47.3 billion — more than $24 billion less than the prior year.

item.title: How global energy production is changing, in 6 charts

item.description: Fossil fuels still dominate global electricity, but wind and solar are surging. In 2025, renewables outpaced coal worldwide for the first time, supplying 34% of electricity.

item.dc:creator: Beshay

item.title: How Americans Are Engaged With News, Politics, Religion and Civic Life
item.dc:creator: Beshay

item.title: Younger and older Americans engage in public life in different ways
item.dc:creator: Beshay
item.description: Older adults are more likely to participate in civic activities like voting, donating or attending religious services, while younger adults engage more in online spaces.

item.title: Democrats and Republicans engage in public life in similar ways
item.dc:creator: Beshay
item.description: Each of the two major parties includes people who are deeply involved in public life – across politics, community, religion and news – and those who are less so.

item.title: Engagement in public life is linked with Americans’ views of politics, news
item.dc:creator: Beshay

item.title: Highly engaged Americans know more about politics
item.dc:creator: Beshay
